title: The Last Human Code Review: Building Trust in AI-Generated Code — Itamar Friedman, Qodo
talk_summary: A Qodo CEO argues the bottleneck in AI-generated code is no longer model capability but context: codified rules, standards, architecture graphs, and tribal knowledge from PR history and incidents. He proposes building a shared context engine usable by both humans and agents, then gradually automating PR approve/block decisions as human comment volume drops.

takeaways.what_they_do: Collect team rules, standards, and skills into one governed context store, then surface which rules were applied and violated during each review, with links for humans to audit.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Codo used four rules. Uh sorry, uh used uh uh many rules and four are violated and that includes a link to all the rules

takeaways.technique: Agent-to-agent review handoff with pre-fixed PR
takeaways.what_they_do: Reviewer agent posts findings, spawns a background fix task (e.g., Claude Code harness) producing a closed fix PR, so the next reviewing agent cherry-picks from passing code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Codo already spend uh uh like uh some back background task and use cloud code for example harness in order to do fixes and there is a closed PR

takeaways.what_they_do: Encode explicit semantic rules for when to approve or block a PR, and add them incrementally over time rather than letting the model decide freely.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to do that not just by letting AI some like choose by yourself, rather giving some semantic rules

takeaways.technique: Rule-usage analytics and PR-comment decay as readiness signal
takeaways.what_they_do: Track how often each rule/skill fires and whether it was useful, and watch developer comment volume on PRs as the metric for when human review can be removed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: developers are writing less and less comments in the pull request. And then after 100 of these pull requests, there's human no more human review

takeaways.technique: Software graph with contracts and incident history
takeaways.what_they_do: Build a graph of repos/microservices where edges carry contracts and links to past discussions and root-cause incidents, so reviews can flag cross-service contract breaks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when a microservice uh one changed its contract and broke a microservice two, right? That is does not exist in most code review

takeaways.technique: Learn from accepted/rejected PRs and discussions
takeaways.what_they_do: Continuously ingest PR history, review discussions, and production-breaking cases into the context store so review judgment improves over time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: learning from PR history, learning from accepted and unaccepted learning from discussions between between developers
